name: PixiTween Director S12a: crew core (contracts, job board, scheduler, snapshots, storyboard ops, inbox, budget)
description: The deterministic heart of the Muse crew: the new crew contracts and events, an abort signal through the Meta HTTP core, pure storyboard ops and scene snapshots, the per-film inbox, job board and scheduler (4 workers, one writer per scene, user first, supersede with rollback) and the budget. No model calls and no UI: the showrunner (S12b), workers (S12c) and UI (S12d) build on this.

readFirst: docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md (sections 3, 4, 4a, 4b and section 7, decisions D-17 to D-23)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-12-crew-swarm/design.md (sections 4 and 5 are the algorithms these stories implement)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-01-meta-api-probes/findings.md (Spark request shapes; the Wonder probe reuses them)
extraGuardrails: Every change under shared/ is additive: new optional fields, new event types, one new enum value ('wonder'). Existing events and fields keep their exact shape, and every existing test must still pass unchanged.
server/crew/storyboard-ops.ts, scene-snapshot.ts and sync.ts are pure: no I/O, no Date.now() inside the functions (pass time in), no mutation of inputs (structuredClone first).
The scheduler never calls a model. Workers are injected as functions so tests use fakes.
manualGates: MG-1: owner runs `npm run live -- s12-wonder` (prints the estimate, about $0.30, ceiling $1), then with `--yes`. Record in the PR: HTTP status, tool-call validity over 5 runs, parallel calls per turn, latency per turn and cost per turn from usage. Choose SHOWRUNNER_MODEL from the result (design 09 section 5).

stories.title: Live probe script for Muse Wonder as a tool-calling showrunner
stories.description: As a owner, I want a one-command probe of Muse Wonder's tool calling so that I can decide with numbers whether it leads the crew.
steps: Read scripts/live/run.ts, scripts/live/s02-smoke.ts (the { describe, estimateUsd, run } shape) and server/meta/spark.ts (the /chat/completions request with tools).
Read docs/hackathon/09-crew-swarm.md section 5 (the five checks and their pass marks) and design.md section 6.3 (the board tool list).

Create scripts/live/s12-wonder.ts exporting describe(), estimateUsd() returning 0.3, and run(). run() builds a Spark client with model process.env.SHOWRUNNER_MODEL ?? 'muse-wonder-1.0' and sends 5 planning turns: a short brief for a fictional cold-brew can, the board tools setStyleBible, reviseStoryboard, dispatch and say as JSON-schema tools, and the system line 'You may call several tools in one turn'.

For each run record: HTTP status, ms, number of tool calls, how many have arguments that parse as JSON and pass a zod check of the tool's params, how many dispatch calls arrived in the same turn, and usage tokens; price them at $4 in / $20 out per 1M tokens.
Print a table of the 5 runs plus totals, and write the redacted results (no headers, no keys) to debug/s12a/wonder-probe.json.
Add scripts/live/s12-wonder.test.ts that imports the module and checks describe() mentions 'Wonder' and estimateUsd() is 0.3, with no network use.
acceptance: scripts/live/s12-wonder.ts exports describe, estimateUsd and run, and estimateUsd() returns 0.3
The dispatcher prints the estimate and exits without a request when --yes is absent (covered by the existing run.test.ts pattern)
The probe's zod checks for the four board tools live in the script and reject an args object missing a required field (unit test with a hand-written args object)

stories.title: Crew contract types in shared/crew.ts
stories.description: As a crew module, I want one shared definition of jobs, lanes, the style bible, storyboard ops and inbox items so that server and web agree.
steps: Read design.md section 4 and shared/storyboard.ts (sceneSchema).

Create shared/crew.ts with zod schemas and inferred types for Lane, JobKind, WRITING_KINDS, JobStatus, JobOrigin, Job, StyleBible, StoryboardOp and InboxItem exactly as design.md section 4, including the length limits (brief <= 600, reason <= 200, summary <= 300, bible fields as listed).
Export JOB_PRIORITY: a function (job) => number implementing design.md section 5.1 (user 0, fix 1, writing kinds 2, take 3, critique and continuity 4).
Create shared/crew.test.ts with a valid example of each schema and one invalid case per schema.
acceptance: styleBibleSchema rejects a palette entry 'orange' and accepts ['#1f2937', '#f59e0b']
storyboardOpSchema accepts { op: 'move', sceneId: 's2', after: null } and rejects { op: 'move', sceneId: 's2' }
JOB_PRIORITY returns 0 for an origin 'user' build and 4 for an 'auto' critique
WRITING_KINDS contains 'restyle-scene' and does not contain 'critique' or 'take'

stories.title: New crew events in the FilmEvent union
stories.description: As a UI and the replay, I want typed crew events so that every crew action is visible and replayable.
steps: Read shared/events.ts and design.md section 4 (the nine new event types).

Edit shared/events.ts: add the event objects crew.agent, job.update, showrunner.heard, showrunner.say, storyboard.revised, style.bible, take.ready, capture.request and budget to filmEventSchema, importing the schemas from shared/crew.ts.
Add 'wonder' to the agent.turn backend enum. Change nothing else in the existing events.
Add shared/events.crew.test.ts parsing one example of each new event with filmEventSchema and checking makeEvent fills `at`.
acceptance: filmEventSchema.parse of a job.update event with a valid Job succeeds, and one whose job.status is 'paused' fails
An agent.turn event with backend 'wonder' parses
All existing tests that use shared/events.ts pass unchanged

stories.title: FilmState crew fields and store support
stories.description: As a crew, I want films to carry crew, parentId, styleBible and storyboardRev so that crew films, takes and storyboard revisions persist.
steps: Read shared/composition.ts (FilmState), shared/ports.ts (FilmStore.create and update) and server/store/film-store.ts.
Edit shared/composition.ts: add optional crew?: boolean, parentId?: FilmId, styleBible?: StyleBible and storyboardRev?: number to FilmState.
Edit shared/ports.ts and server/store/film-store.ts so create() accepts crew and parentId, and update() accepts styleBible and storyboardRev alongside status, storyboard and title.
Extend server/store/film-store.test.ts: create with parentId round-trips through get(); update with storyboardRev 3 round-trips; a film written before this change (no new fields) still loads.
acceptance: films.create({ ...init, parentId: 'f_parent', crew: false }) then films.get(id) returns parentId 'f_parent'
films.update(id, { storyboardRev: 3 }) then get(id).storyboardRev === 3
A film.json without the new fields loads with crew undefined and the existing film-store tests pass

stories.title: Crew env keys
stories.description: As a owner, I want the crew's knobs validated in one place so that a bad value fails at boot.
steps: Read server/env.ts, its test and .env.example.

Edit server/env.ts: add CREW_ENABLED (boolean, default true), SHOWRUNNER_MODEL (string, default 'muse-wonder-1.0'), CREW_MAX_WORKERS (int 1-8, default 4), CREW_FILM_BUDGET_USD (number 0.1-20, default 1.5), CREW_TAKES_MAX (int 2-3, default 3), CREW_INBOX_DEBOUNCE_MS (int 0-10000, default 1500), CREW_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS (int 5000-600000, default 90000), CREW_IDLE_END_MS (int 60000-3600000, default 600000).
Add the same keys with their defaults and a one-line comment each to .env.example.
Extend server/env.test.ts for the defaults and for CREW_MAX_WORKERS=9 being rejected.
acceptance: loadEnv() with none of the keys set returns CREW_MAX_WORKERS 4 and SHOWRUNNER_MODEL 'muse-wonder-1.0'
CREW_MAX_WORKERS=9 makes env validation throw an error that names CREW_MAX_WORKERS
CREW_ENABLED=false parses to the boolean false

stories.title: Abort signal through the Meta HTTP core and LlmBackend
stories.description: As a scheduler, I want to stop a worker's in-flight model call so that a superseded job costs at most one call.
steps: Read server/meta/http.ts, shared/ports.ts (LlmBackend.chatWithTools opts), shared/tools.ts (ToolCtx) and server/llm/spark-backend.ts.

Edit server/meta/http.ts: json(), form() and sse() accept an optional { signal?: AbortSignal } last argument and pass it to fetch; an aborted request rejects with an error whose name is 'AbortError' and is never retried.
Edit shared/ports.ts: chatWithTools opts gain signal?: AbortSignal; edit shared/tools.ts: ToolCtx gains signal?: AbortSignal and scope?: { sceneId: string }.
Edit server/llm/spark-backend.ts and the Spark client call path so the signal reaches http.json.
Add server/meta/http.abort.test.ts with a local node:http server that delays 2 s: aborting after 50 ms rejects within 500 ms with name 'AbortError', and the server saw exactly one request.
acceptance: An aborted json() call rejects with err.name === 'AbortError' in under 500 ms against a 2 s server
An aborted call is not retried (the test server counts 1 request)
Calls without a signal behave as before (existing http tests pass)

stories.title: Pure storyboard ops with stable ids and dirty kinds
stories.description: As a showrunner and the user, I want to add, update, remove and move scenes so that the storyboard can change mid-build.
steps: Read design.md section 5.4 (the op table and the stable-id rule) and shared/storyboard.ts.

Create server/crew/storyboard-ops.ts exporting applyOps(storyboard, ops): { storyboard, dirty: Record<string, Array<'rebuild' | 'camera' | 'text' | 'duration' | 'mode'>>, added: string[], removed: string[] } and nextSceneId(storyboard, removedIds) returning 's<max+1>' over current and removed ids.
Validate the result with storyboardSchema and the max-2-generate rule; on failure throw StoryboardOpError with the zod message and apply nothing.
Create server/crew/storyboard-ops.test.ts covering every row of the design table.
acceptance: Adding a scene after 's2' to [s1, s2, s3] gives the order [s1, s2, s4, s3], the new id 's4' and dirty { s4: ['rebuild'] }
After removing 's3' from [s1, s2, s3], an add gives the new id 's4', not 's3'
An update of only camera on s2 gives dirty { s2: ['camera'] }; an update of intent gives ['rebuild']
Ops that make 7 scenes, or a total over 30 s, throw StoryboardOpError and the input storyboard is unchanged

stories.title: Pure scene snapshot, restore and splice
stories.description: As a scheduler, I want to roll a scene back and to splice a take in so that a cancelled or replaced job never damages other scenes.
steps: Read design.md section 5.3, docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 3a (meta.director, layer ids) and server/authoring/api.ts (setSceneDuration).
Create server/crew/scene-snapshot.ts exporting snapshotScene(comp, sceneId), restoreScene(comp, sceneId, snap) and spliceScene(target, sceneId, source) as in the design; all three return new objects.
Create server/crew/scene-snapshot.test.ts using the fixture composition from fixtures/s03a (two scenes) plus layers added with the authoring core.
acceptance: snapshot s1, add three layers to s1, restore: the s1 precomp deep-equals the snapshot and s2 is unchanged (deep equal)
Restoring a 4 s snapshot onto a scene now 6 s long shifts s2's start back by 60 frames at 30 fps
spliceScene copies the source scene's layers, meta.director entries and referenced asset entries into the target
The input compositions are not mutated (structuredClone comparison)

stories.title: Deterministic storyboard-to-composition sync
stories.description: As a crew, I want storyboard changes that need no model to apply at once so that camera, text and duration edits are instant.
steps: Read design.md section 5.4 (sync column), server/authoring/api.ts and server/crew/storyboard-ops.ts.

Create server/crew/sync.ts exporting syncComposition(comp, before, after, result): { next, needsBuilder: string[] }: add (addScene then swaps into position), remove (removeScene), move (swaps), duration (setSceneDuration), camera (setCamera), text (setText on '<sceneId>:headline', adding a text layer if missing). Mode changes are returned in needsMode: string[] and not applied here.
Create server/crew/sync.test.ts for each change kind.
acceptance: A camera-only change on s2 to 'pan' returns needsBuilder [] and s2's camera keys are those of setCamera(c, 's2', 'pan')
Adding s4 after s2 puts the s4 precomp layer third in the root timeline and returns needsBuilder ['s4']
A text change on s1 with no headline layer adds 's1:headline' with that text

stories.title: Per-film inbox with immediate user wake and debounced job wake
stories.description: As a showrunner loop, I want inbox items batched sensibly so that four finishing builders cost one turn but a user message is heard at once.
steps: Read design.md section 5.6.

Create server/crew/inbox.ts exporting createInbox({ debounceMs, maxWaitMs = 5000, now? }) with push(item) and drain(): Promise<InboxItem[]>; drain resolves at once when a 'user' item is pending, otherwise debounceMs after the last arrival and at most maxWaitMs after the first.
Create server/crew/inbox.test.ts using vi.useFakeTimers.
acceptance: With debounceMs 1500, three job items pushed 200 ms apart resolve one drain with all three, 1500 ms after the third
A user item resolves a pending drain within the same tick, together with any job items already queued
Items pushed every 1 s for 10 s are delivered no later than 5000 ms after the first item

stories.title: Job board with transitions, events and persistence
stories.description: As a UI and the replay, I want every job transition recorded and announced so that the crew board is always truthful.
steps: Read design.md sections 4 and 5.2, server/events/bus.ts and server/store/film-store.ts (atomic writes).

Create server/crew/board.ts exporting createBoard({ filmId, emit, persist, now }) with add(partialJob) (assigns ids 'j1', 'j2', …), get(id), list(), update(id, patch) and allowed transitions queued -> running | superseded | cancelled, running -> awaiting-frames | done | failed | superseded | cancelled, awaiting-frames -> done | failed | cancelled. Every change emits job.update with the full job.
Create server/crew/persist.ts writing data/films/<id>/crew/board.json atomically and reading it back.
Create server/crew/test-helpers.ts with makeTestBoard() over a temp dir, and server/crew/board.test.ts.
acceptance: add() twice returns ids 'j1' and 'j2' and emits two job.update events
update('j1', { status: 'done' }) from 'queued' throws an error naming the transition
A board reloaded from board.json lists the same jobs with the same statuses

stories.title: Scheduler: worker cap, one writer per scene, priority, dependsOn
stories.description: As a crew, I want jobs to start in the right order so that four scenes build at once and the user's request goes first.
steps: Read design.md section 5.1 and shared/crew.ts (JOB_PRIORITY, WRITING_KINDS).

Create server/crew/scheduler.ts exporting createScheduler({ board, maxWorkers, runWorker, budget? }) where runWorker(job, signal) is injected; pump() starts runnable jobs per the design pseudo-code; a finished worker marks the job done or failed (with its summary or error) and calls pump() again.
Create server/crew/scheduler.test.ts with fake workers that resolve on demand.
acceptance: Six queued build jobs on six scenes with maxWorkers 4 give exactly 4 running; finishing one starts the fifth
A second writing job on scene s1 does not start while s1 has a running writer, while a job on s2 does
With one slot free, a user-origin restyle queued after three auto builds starts first
A critique on s1 does not start while a writing job on s1 is queued or running

stories.title: Supersede and cancel with scene rollback
stories.description: As a user, I want my newer request to replace the work in progress on that scene so that I never wait for a build I no longer want.
steps: Read design.md sections 5.2 and 5.3, server/crew/scheduler.ts and server/crew/scene-snapshot.ts.

Edit server/crew/scheduler.ts: dispatch(job) applies the supersede rules; cancel(jobId) aborts the job's AbortController, awaits the worker, then calls films.mutate(filmId, c => restoreScene(c, sceneId, snapshot), 'director', 'rollback <jobId>'). The snapshot is taken with snapshotScene just before a writing job starts and written to data/films/<id>/crew/snapshots/<jobId>.json.
Extend server/crew/scheduler.test.ts with makeTestFilm and a fake builder that commits one layer per tick and checks signal.aborted between ticks.
acceptance: A user restyle on s1 while a fake builder on s1 has committed 2 layers: the builder ends 'superseded' with supersededBy the new job id, and s1 deep-equals its pre-job snapshot before the restyle starts
Scene s2, built by another fake worker during the rollback, is unchanged by it
A queued build on s1 becomes 'superseded' and a queued critique on s1 becomes 'cancelled'
A showrunner-origin 'edit' on s1 waits for the running s1 builder instead of cancelling it

stories.title: Producer: per-film budget with warn and stop
stories.description: As a owner, I want each film's spend capped so that a chatty crew can't drain the Meta credits.
steps: Read design.md section 5.11, server/ledger.ts and server/crew/scheduler.ts.

Create server/crew/budget.ts exporting createBudget({ ledger, filmId, childFilmIds: () => string[], capUsd, emit }) with spent(), estimate(job) (the static table in the design), allows(job) and check() which emits a budget event when the level changes (ok -> warn at 80 %, -> stop at 100 %).
Edit server/crew/scheduler.ts so a job that budget.allows() refuses is marked failed with error 'budget'.
Create server/crew/budget.test.ts.
acceptance: With cap 1.0 and 0.79 spent, a build (est 0.03) is allowed and the level stays 'ok'; at 0.80 spent a budget event with level 'warn' is emitted once
With 0.99 spent, a take (est 0.03) is refused and its job fails with error 'budget'
Spend recorded on a child film counts toward the parent
